Dexamfetamin (ATC code N06BA02) is a stimulant medication used in the pharmacological treatment of ADHD. Within the Danish national ADHD database quality monitoring system, it is tracked as one of the specific medications used to calculate key clinical quality indicators.

Specifically, Dexamfetamin is one of six ADHD medications included in the calculation of [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], which measures pharmacological treatment coverage among ADHD patients in standard care pathways [^src1] [^src2]. This indicator is used to evaluate the systemic balance between pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment components across different Danish regions and departments [^src2]. 

As the national database expanded its scope to include adult patients, Dexamfetamin was also incorporated into the newly introduced [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] [^src3]. This indicator measures pharmacological treatment for adults with ADHD, utilizing registry data to monitor clinical practices [^src3]. In this adult treatment context, Dexamfetamin is evaluated alongside other specific medications, including methylphenidate, modafinil, atomoxetine, lisdexamfetamine, and guanfacine [^src3].
